title: Selector v2 telemetry: decision metrics/events, sampling, bucketing, trace annotations
creator: Grace Kim
description:
Goal
Add production-safe telemetry for kernel selector v2 so we can:
- Debug “why this kernel was chosen” (model family, seq regime, GPU SKU, selector version, rule/override path)
- Correlate decision outcomes with latency/cost/correctness (incl. NaNs / shape mismatches)
- Monitor rollout safely (selector_v2 vs v1 split; fallback frequency; unknown model handling)
- Avoid blowing up metrics cardinality (controlled labels + bucketing + sampling)

Scope
1) Metrics (Prometheus-style) required for selector v2 rollout and ongoing perf/regression analysis
2) Structured event logs (sampled) for deep dives, linked to trace/span IDs
3) Trace annotations (OpenTelemetry attributes) on request spans and kernel execution spans
4) Sampling & cardinality controls aligned with platform standards

Non-goals
- Building new dashboards (tracked in ENG-3933 / INT-2331)
- Changing customer-facing API behavior

Proposed instrumentation
A) Metrics (required)
- counter: runtime_kernel_selector_decisions_total
  Labels (strict allowlist):
  - selector_version: {"v1","v2"}
  - decision_outcome: {"selected","fallback_v1","fallback_safe_set","override","error"}
  - model_family: enum (see registry taxonomy; "unknown" allowed)
  - seq_bucket: {"prefill_s","prefill_m","prefill_l","decode_s","decode_m","decode_l"} (exact buckets below)
  - gpu_sku: normalized enum {"L4","A10","A100","H100","OTHER"}
  - kernel_id: short stable id (bucketed; see kernel_id bucketing below)
  - tier: {"hosted","dedicated","private"}
- counter: runtime_kernel_selector_unknown_model_family_total
  Labels: selector_version, gpu_sku, tier
- counter: runtime_kernel_selector_registry_miss_total
  (registry has no matching row/column)
  Labels: selector_version, model_family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket, tier
- counter: runtime_kernel_selector_fallback_total
  Labels: selector_version, fallback_reason, model_family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket, tier
  fallback_reason enum:
  {"unknown_family","missing_metadata","gpu_unsupported","shape_unsupported","conformance_blocked","registry_miss","override_disabled_v2"}
- histogram: runtime_kernel_selector_decision_latency_ms
  Labels: selector_version, tier
  Notes: do NOT label by model_family/gpu/kernel_id; keep low-cardinality.
- gauge: runtime_kernel_registry_version
  Labels: tier
  Value: semantic/monotonic registry version loaded in process (also log on boot)

Kernel ID labeling / bucketing
- Kernel IDs can be high cardinality if we include full internal names. For metrics, we will use:
  - kernel_id: stable short token (e.g., "attn_fa2_v3", "attn_xformers_v2", "attn_safe_v1")
  - kernel_variant: (optional) {"default","gqa","longctx"} if needed, but only if we can keep it within a small bounded set.
- Full kernel identifier (including commit hash / compile flags) goes only in sampled events/logs, not metric labels.

Sequence length buckets (agreed with Scheduling)
We need deterministic, low-cardinality buckets based on selector input context.
- regime = prefill vs decode (from scheduler signal)
- effective_seq_len = prompt_len for prefill; context_len for decode (as provided by scheduler/runtime boundary)
Buckets:
- prefill_s: [0, 512]
- prefill_m: (512, 2048]
- prefill_l: (2048, 8192]
- decode_s: [0, 128]
- decode_m: (128, 512]
- decode_l: (512, 2048]
Note: anything > max bucket should clamp into *_l to avoid unbounded label values.

GPU SKU normalization
- Use normalized sku string from ENG-3925 (e.g., "NVIDIA_L4" -> "L4")
- If unknown/unmapped, label gpu_sku="OTHER" and include raw sku only in sampled events.

Model family bucketing
- model_family is from ENG-3922/ENG-3926 taxonomy. Allow only:
  {"llama","mistral","qwen","gemma","mixtral","phi","unknown","other"}
- Any new family must be added to allowlist + registry mapping to avoid exploding cardinality.

B) Tracing (OpenTelemetry)
Attach attributes to the request span (or the “inference” span) and to a child “kernel_exec” span if available.
Required attributes on request span:
- redwood.selector.version: "v1" | "v2"
- redwood.selector.decision_outcome: enum from above
- redwood.selector.model_family: allowlisted string
- redwood.selector.seq_bucket: allowlisted string
- redwood.selector.gpu_sku: allowlisted string
- redwood.selector.kernel_id: short stable id (same as metric label)
- redwood.selector.override_source: {"none","config_model_family","config_model_exact","emergency_kill_switch"}
- redwood.selector.fallback_reason: enum (only if fallback)
- redwood.registry.version: loaded registry version
- redwood.selector.explain_code: short reason code (e.g., "R_MATCH_EXACT", "R_MATCH_WILDCARD", "R_FALLBACK_SAFE", "R_OVERRIDE")

PII/sensitive
- Do not attach raw model name, customer id, org name, prompt length exact value, or raw GPU uuid as attributes.
- If needed for debugging, raw values go to sampled structured logs with appropriate redaction and access controls.

C) Structured events (sampled)
Emit a structured log event “kernel_selector_decision” with:
- timestamp, request_id, trace_id, span_id
- selector_version, registry_version
- model_family, model_name_hash (stable hash only; no raw string)
- seq_regime (prefill/decode), effective_seq_len_bucket, effective_seq_len_clamped
- gpu_sku_norm, gpu_sm (optional), mig_mode (boolean) if available from ENG-3925
- kernel_id_short, kernel_id_full
- decision_path: list of steps (strings) with bounded length (max 8 steps)
- fallback_reason / override_source

Sampling policy
- Success path: 0.5–1% sampling (configurable); ensure per-process rate limit.
- Always log on:
  - decision_outcome != "selected" (fallback/override/error)
  - conformance guard triggered / NaN guard triggered
  - unknown model family or registry miss
- For canary/rollout, allow temporary bump of sampling (e.g., 5%) gated by region + tier config; default back to 1% post-rollout.

Acceptance criteria
- Runtime exposes metrics above (names final per telemetry standards doc) and they are visible in staging + one canary region.
- Traces for sampled requests include selector attributes; verified in trace viewer.
- Cardinality review: label values bounded and verified via staging load test; no per-model-name or per-customer labels.
- Metrics can power SRE guardrails: selector version split, fallback rate, unknown family rate, decision latency.

Implementation notes / pointers
- Follow: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/kernel-selection-telemetry-standards.json
- Coordinate with: Thomas Baird (cardinality), Allison Grant (observability standards), Aisha Bello (dashboards/alerts), Omar El-Sayed (runtime integration)
- Ensure selector v1/v2 parity in telemetry fields to enable comparisons during rollout.

Open questions
1) Do we need to distinguish attention kernel vs prefill kernel vs decode kernel in kernel_id? Proposal: kernel_id encodes op family (attn/prefill/decode) already; avoid extra labels unless necessary.
2) Where to attach “kernel_exec” span attributes in runtime? If too invasive, put all selector fields on request span and add a single "kernel_id" attribute on the kernel callsite.
3) Should “tier” be labeled in metrics or derived from deployment? Proposal: keep tier label; it’s bounded and helpful for Dedicated/Hosted comparison.
